doc.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: First Chicago winter and the heavy snow
summary: On his first winter in Chicago snow piled ten feet high, men shoveled streets, and he was well dressed for it.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: We were going back through the schools. The first school was Douglas Elementary?
That was when you just arrived, I would imagine.
Do you recall going there with your mom or . . .?

I remember being taken there with my – by my mother. It was my first winter in Chicago. I recall that it snowed so bad – so strongly and so bad, you couldn’t see from one side of the street to the other. We didn’t have these modern snow plows and all that. They had men out there with shovels trying to get you in and out of your doorways. This was – everything stopped. It wasn’t – you couldn’t go to school. You couldn’t do nothing. But I recall that the winter in Chicago was something else. The snow was . . .
This was a blizzard, I would imagine. It was how – you were a small one. Do you recall how high the snow piles were?

They were so high you could not see across the street. I would say 10 feet – 10 or 12 feet high. I mean stacked up. They had men out there with shovels. They got paid. That’s when the city would pay them with shovels, get the shovels to shovel the streets, so you could get through there. It was not too far removed from the horse and buggy days, really. It’s really rough. The weather is something else.
But for you, you were fairly young and you were adapting to the weather?

Yeah. In fact, it was fun at first. Out there – I never saw snow before. Out there with the snow. I was well – here again, the family had to be pretty well – they weren’t poor, because I was well dressed and well taken care of for it – for the weather. I was ready for it. I don’t recall ever – sometimes people talk about how cold it is and you didn’t have the right clothes to wear. We had – I had everything – everything was right. Never had any want for anything like that.
